analysis.title: Fed Review – Fed pauses, but tightening cycle is not over
key_insights: The Fed left policy rates unchanged at 3.75-4.00% at its October meeting, in line with consensus and Danske's expectations. Two members dissented in favour of a rate hike (10-2 vote).

Danske reads Warsh's press conference comments on the economic outlook as hawkish even though the market reaction was dovish. He said growth had strengthened, with Q3 growth above 3%, strong consumption growth, and business investment probably rising by a double-digit percentage.
Danske maintains its call for two 25bp hikes at the December 2026 and March 2027 meetings and sees risks tilted toward more than two hikes.
The statement wording was largely unchanged from September, with a slight hawkish shift from 'economic activity is expanding at a solid pace' to 'expanding at a strong pace'.

Warsh gave no specific comments on the future rate path. He several times flagged the tightening of financial conditions since September, which Danske cites as its main argument for why the Fed could wait before delivering the next hike.
Warsh appears to prefer more data points between rate decisions. Danske says this slightly supports its call for gradual hikes with pauses rather than hikes at back-to-back meetings.
If inflation shows further signs of broadening and underlying inflation increases more rapidly, Danske thinks the Fed will hike at back-to-back meetings.

The FOMC will change the format of some meetings from autumn 2027. One meeting in autumn 2027 will have no rate decision, and from 2028 two of the eight annual meetings will not include a rate decision. The affected meetings were not specified. Danske says this further supports gradual hikes over back-to-back moves.

Warsh flagged details on the five task forces he created. Some, but not all, will have recommendations by the year-end deadline. The productivity task force holds a hearing on 16 November and the balance sheet task force will have recommendations in early Q1.

Markets now price 21bp for the December meeting, down from 23-24bp before the press conference. The next hike is fully priced only by April, previously March. The UST curve steepened as front-end rates dropped and breakeven inflation expectations rose.
EUR/USD spot rose back above 1.1150 while the forward curve declined slightly. Danske keeps its bearish EUR/USD view with a 6-12M target of 1.10.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Matched Danske's preview call of 2-3 dissenters. Hammack was expected to dissent, Cook was not. Cook's dissent widens the group of voters willing to dissent.

trade_ideas.rationale: Danske expects two more Fed hikes in December and March, supporting the dollar.

risk_factors: Inflation broadening and underlying inflation rising faster could lead the Fed to hike at back-to-back meetings, which would mean more than two hikes.
Tightening of financial conditions since September, flagged by Warsh several times, is Danske's main argument for why the Fed could wait before the next hike.
The affected meetings under the new no-decision format are unspecified, which leaves the timing of later hikes uncertain.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: Warsh described strong growth, consumption and double-digit business investment growth, and the Fed will not be afraid to hike at back-to-back meetings if inflation broadens. Danske sees risks tilted to more than two hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish case: Warsh gave no commitment to a December hike, flagged tighter financial conditions since September, and prefers more data points between decisions. The market priced December down to 21bp and the next hike only by April.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further signs of broadening inflation and a faster rise in underlying inflation would lead the Fed to hike at back-to-back meetings.
